Consult Summary:
- Left elbow swelling for about one week, suspected bursitis; NSAID therapy started and blood tests ordered to evaluate inflammatory/infectious/rheumatologic causes; follow-up planned to review results (in clinic, by phone, or by video).

History:
- Presenting complaint: Swelling of the left elbow noticed about one week ago. Not painful; patient feels fine aside from the unusual swelling. The area is slightly warm with a sensation of some fluid inside. No clear history of injury or trauma.
- Timeline and progression: Onset about one week ago. Currently described as “a bit better” by the patient; no marked progression reported.
- Exacerbating, initiating, or relieving factors: No injury reported; no prior episodes. No medication-related relief noted prior to visit.
- Associated symptoms: No systemic symptoms reported. Skin around the swelling noted as dry; no eczema or other rheumatologic history reported by patient.
- Systems review and negatives: No fever, no significant joint pain elsewhere mentioned. Patient remains mobile and able to move the elbow.
- Relevant negatives: No history of rheumatic disease in family reported; patient did have a prior GP-confirmed diagnosis of osteoarthritis a few years ago.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis diagnosed by a GP a few years ago.
- Allergies: peanuts.
- Medications: none regularly.

Social History:
- Occupation: desk-based work.
- Physical activity: runs regularly, about 2–3 times per week.
- Tobacco, alcohol, or substance use: not documented.
- Other lifestyle factors: not documented.

Family History:
- No known rheumatologic diseases in the family.
- Patient has history of osteoarthritis; family history of OA not clearly documented.

Physical Examination:
- Left elbow with swelling; skin over the area was slightly warm and dry (tip of elbow notably dry).
- Range of motion: patient can move elbow normally.
- Tenderness: not severely tender on palpation; no signs of septic arthritis observed during examination.
- Other exam findings: Dry skin noted; no widespread skin or systemic clues noted.

Investigations:
- Plan: Blood tests to screen for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout.
  - Blood test forms to be sent to patient’s home with instructions for sampling.
  - Expected time to results: about 5–6 days after testing.
- Additional testing or imaging not performed at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left elbow swelling likely bursitis (inflammation of a fluid-filled sac around the joint).
  - Plan:
    - Initiate NSAID therapy: Ibuprofen 400 mg by mouth twice daily after meals; discontinue if heartburn occurs.
    - Advise monitoring for improvement over several days.

- Issue 2: Rule out infection or other systemic/ rheumatologic causes of joint swelling.
  - Plan:
    - Obtain blood tests for inflammatory markers, infectious screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout screen.
    - Blood tests to be completed at home with results reviewed after completion.
    - Schedule a follow-up appointment (clinic, telephone, or video) to review blood test results and reassess the elbow.

- Issue 3: Safety and red-flag guidance.
  - Plan:
    - Instruct patient to seek urgent evaluation (phone/video contact or emergency care) if elbow becomes very red, very painful, if redness spreads, or if there is rapid worsening.

- Overall follow-up:
  - Blood test results anticipated in about 5–6 days; follow-up after results to decide on further management.
  - If symptoms worsen or new red flags appear sooner, contact the clinic for sooner assessment.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (not provided).
  - Comprehensive medication reconciliation beyond current context (patient reports no regular meds; allergies noted).
  - Vaccination status or other preventive health data (not documented).
  - Smoking, alcohol, and substance use details (not documented).
- Internal conflicts:
  - None detected in the transcript.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; some minor conversational filler and repetitions, but no major obscurities affecting content.

Document quality notes:
- Allergies: peanut allergy documented.
- Current medications: none documented.
- No vitals available. No imaging performed. No definitive imaging to support diagnosis beyond exam.
- Allergen/medication notes consistent with transcript.
